src.q: Ono was born and grew up in Tokyo and moved to New York City in 1952 to join her family.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
src.q: After leaving college Ono moved to New York in 1957, supporting herself through secretarial work and lessons in the traditional Japanese arts at the Japan Society.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
notes.q: Ono would enact many of the book's scenarios as performance pieces throughout her career, which formed the basis for her art exhibitions, including the highly publicized retrospective exhibition, This Is Not Here in 1971 at the Everson Museum in Syracuse, New York, that was nearly closed when it was besieged by excited Beatles fans, who broke several of the art pieces and flooded the toilets.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
src.q: After the Beatles disbanded in 1970, Ono and Lennon lived together in London and then moved permanently to Manhattan to escape tabloid racism towards Ono.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
notes.q: In 1989, the Whitney Museum held a retrospective of her work, Yoko Ono: Objects, Films, marking Ono's reentry into the New York art world after a hiatus.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
notes.q: In a Rolling Stone interview in 1987, Ono pointed out McCartney's place in the disintegration of the band.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
src.q: In 1987, Ono travelled to Moscow to participate in the "International Forum for a Nuclear-free World and for the Survival of Mankind".

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
notes.q: In 2008, she showed a large retrospective exhibition, Between The Sky and My Head, at the Kunsthalle Bielefeld, Bielefeld, Germany, and the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art in Gateshead, England.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yoko Ono
notes.q: She also received a Golden Lion Award for lifetime achievement from the Venice Biennale in 2009.

src.q: Ono returned to Liverpool for the 2008 Liverpool Biennial, where she unveiled Sky Ladders in the ruins of Church of St Luke (which was largely destroyed during World War II and now stands roofless as a memorial to those killed in the Liverpool Blitz).
